questions.stem: In MS Word, which keyboard shortcut is used to save a document?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + S saves the active document in MS Word (and across most applications). Ctrl + P opens the Print dialog, Ctrl + V pastes, and Ctrl + X cuts. These universal shortcuts are frequently tested in computer-awareness sections.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What is the default file extension of an MS Word document (in modern versions)?
questions.explanation: The default extension for MS Word documents (Word 2007 onwards) is .docx. The older format was .doc. Excel uses .xlsx (older .xls), PowerPoint uses .pptx (older .ppt), and .pdf is a portable document format not native to a single Office app.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, a single rectangular box formed by the intersection of a row and a column is called a:
questions.explanation: A cell is the basic unit of an Excel worksheet, formed where a row (numbered) and a column (lettered) intersect, e.g., 'A1'. A range is a group of cells; a worksheet is a single sheet of cells; a workbook is the entire Excel file containing one or more worksheets.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, every formula must begin with which symbol?
questions.explanation: Every formula in MS Excel must begin with the equals sign (=), e.g., =SUM(A1:A10) or =A1+B1. This tells Excel to treat the entry as a formula to calculate rather than as plain text. Functions like SUM, AVERAGE, and IF all follow the = sign.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS PowerPoint, a single page of a presentation is called a:
questions.explanation: In MS PowerPoint, each individual page is called a slide. A collection of slides forms a presentation. Features include slide layouts, transitions (effects between slides), and animations (effects on objects within a slide). Press F5 to start a slideshow from the beginning.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which keyboard shortcut copies selected text or objects to the clipboard?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + C copies the selected content to the clipboard. Ctrl + Z undoes the last action, Ctrl + A selects all, and Ctrl + B applies bold formatting. The copy-paste trio is Ctrl+C (copy), Ctrl+X (cut), Ctrl+V (paste).
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, which function adds up a range of numbers?
questions.explanation: The SUM() function adds up a range of numbers, e.g., =SUM(A1:A10) totals cells A1 through A10. AVERAGE() returns the mean, COUNT() counts numeric entries, and MAX() returns the largest value. SUM is one of the most frequently used Excel functions.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Word, which shortcut key is used to find text within a document?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + F opens the Find tool to search for text in a document. Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace, Ctrl + G opens Go To, and Ctrl + E centre-aligns the selected paragraph. Find (Ctrl+F) is a universal shortcut across most applications and browsers.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, what does the function =AVERAGE(B1:B5) compute?

options.text: The arithmetic mean of cells B1 to B5
The sum of cells B1 to B5
The largest value among B1 to B5
The number of cells from B1 to B5

questions.explanation: =AVERAGE(B1:B5) computes the arithmetic mean (sum divided by count) of the values in cells B1 through B5. To get the sum you'd use SUM(), the largest value MAX(), and the count of numeric cells COUNT(). AVERAGE ignores empty cells and text.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which MS Office application is best suited for creating slide-based presentations?
questions.explanation: MS PowerPoint is designed for creating slide-based presentations. MS Word is for word processing (documents), MS Excel for spreadsheets and calculations, and MS Access for database management. Each Office application serves a distinct primary purpose.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Word, the shortcut Ctrl + Z is used to:
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes the last action. To redo (reverse an undo), use Ctrl + Y. These let users step backward and forward through their editing history. Ctrl+Z is one of the most-used productivity shortcuts.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, what does a cell reference like $A$1 (with dollar signs) represent?

options.text: A relative reference that changes when copied
An absolute reference that does not change when the formula is copied

questions.explanation: $A$1 is an absolute reference — the dollar signs lock both the column (A) and row (1) so the reference does not change when the formula is copied to other cells. A1 (no dollars) is relative and adjusts when copied. A$1 or $A1 are mixed references (locking only row or column). This is a common Excel exam point.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which feature in MS Word automatically corrects common spelling mistakes as you type?
questions.explanation: AutoCorrect automatically fixes common typing and spelling errors (e.g., 'teh' → 'the') as you type. Mail Merge creates personalised letters/labels from a data source; Track Changes records edits for review; Word Count shows the number of words. AutoCorrect can be customised or disabled.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which MS Word feature is used to create personalised copies of a document (like letters) for many recipients from a single template and a data list?
questions.explanation: Mail Merge combines a main document (template) with a data source (such as an Excel list or Outlook contacts) to produce many personalised copies — commonly used for bulk letters, envelopes, labels, and emails. The data source supplies fields like name and address that are inserted into each copy.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, which function counts how many cells in a range contain numbers?
questions.explanation: COUNT() counts the number of cells in a range that contain numbers, e.g., =COUNT(A1:A10). COUNTA() counts non-empty cells (including text); SUM() totals values; LEN() returns the length of a text string; TODAY() returns the current date. COUNT ignores text and empty cells.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What is the keyboard shortcut to make selected text bold in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + B makes selected text bold. Ctrl + I applies italics, and Ctrl + U applies underline. These three formatting shortcuts (B/I/U) are standard across word processors and many applications.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS PowerPoint, which key starts the slideshow from the beginning?
questions.explanation: F5 starts the slideshow from the first slide in MS PowerPoint. Shift + F5 starts from the current slide. F1 opens Help, F12 opens 'Save As', and Esc ends the slideshow. These presentation shortcuts are commonly tested.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, the default name of the first worksheet in a new workbook is typically:
questions.explanation: The default name of the first worksheet is 'Sheet1' (subsequent sheets are Sheet2, Sheet3...). 'Book1' is the default name of the entire workbook (the file), not the sheet. Worksheets can be renamed by double-clicking the sheet tab.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which shortcut in MS Word selects the entire document?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + A selects all content in the document. Ctrl + S saves, Ctrl + E centre-aligns, and Ctrl + W closes the current document/window. 'Select All' (Ctrl+A) works in most applications and file managers.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, which symbol is used to make a cell reference absolute?
questions.explanation: The dollar sign ($) makes a cell reference absolute, e.g., $A$1. The & (ampersand) concatenates text, * is multiplication, and % formats/divides as percentage. Placing $ before the column letter and/or row number locks that part when the formula is copied.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, if cell C1 contains =A1+B1 and is copied to cell C2, what will C2 contain (assuming relative references)?
questions.explanation: With relative references, copying =A1+B1 from C1 down to C2 shifts the row references down by one, giving =A2+B2. Relative references automatically adjust based on the new location. If the references had been absolute ($A$1+$B$1), they would have stayed unchanged.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, which function would you use to return one value if a condition is TRUE and another if it is FALSE?
questions.explanation: The IF() function performs a logical test and returns one value if TRUE and another if FALSE, e.g., =IF(A1>=40,"Pass","Fail"). VLOOKUP() looks up a value in a table; CONCATENATE() (or &) joins text; SUM() totals numbers. IF is the foundation of conditional logic in spreadsheets.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, what does the VLOOKUP function do?

options.text: Counts the number of vowels in a cell
Validates whether a cell contains a valid date
Searches for a value in the leftmost column of a table and returns a value in the same row from a specified column

questions.explanation: VLOOKUP (Vertical Lookup) searches for a value in the leftmost column of a table and returns a corresponding value from a specified column in the same row, e.g., =VLOOKUP(101, A2:D50, 3, FALSE) finds ID 101 and returns the 3rd-column value. The FALSE argument requests an exact match. It is one of the most powerful Excel lookup functions.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Word, 'Track Changes' is primarily used to:

options.text: Count the number of pages automatically
Record insertions, deletions, and edits so reviewers can see and accept/reject each change
Track the location of the document on the hard disk
Automatically save the document at intervals

questions.explanation: Track Changes records every insertion, deletion, and formatting edit made to a document, displaying them as marked revisions. Reviewers and authors can then accept or reject each change individually. It is essential for collaborative editing and document review workflows. Auto-save (option D) is a separate feature.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In MS Excel, what will the formula =LEN("PARIKSHA") return?
questions.explanation: The LEN() function returns the number of characters in a text string. 'PARIKSHA' has 8 letters (P-A-R-I-K-S-H-A), so =LEN("PARIKSHA") returns 8. LEN counts all characters including spaces and punctuation, but the quotation marks delimiting the text are not counted.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
